next_question: Change the level of description a fifth time and change what is being bounded: stop asking WHETHER an inherited mechanism can transfer to an unseen site, and measure THE SIZE OF THE SURFACE OVER WHICH INHERITANCE COULD POSSIBLY AMORTIZE. This packet's deepest result is not about a key or a cache. It is that on the credential-free public HTTP substrate SPIDER can actually observe without credentials, there is very little that only a prior episode can know: the five reachable real sites exposed 0.000 session-scoped identifiers, offered no write verb, and the only identifiers they expose are the sites own public resource ids, which a fresh episode re-reads for about 119 tokens per observation against the audited 763.06-token per-observation floor from EXP-INTEL-36287179392. All 48 C-CROSSSITE events in the Codex and every frontier inheritance packet measured whether a mechanism TRANSFERS; none measured whether there is anything to transfer, and the one measurement attempted here failed on instrument validity rather than returning an answer. The concrete falsifiable question: on real credential-free sites that do have action-gating structure rather than five always-200 JSON endpoints, what FRACTION of action-gating objects is reachable by a single unconditional GET from a root observation and therefore free to re-derive at the established observation floor, versus requires a discovered path and therefore costs cross-episode state, and does that fraction move the sign of the amortization comparison? Preregister with no new infrastructure, stdlib HTTP only, no browser, no docker, no model key: (i) a RE_DERIVABLE arm that discards all prior state and re-reads the root each episode, carrying the audited 763-token structural representation so observation cost is not silently discarded; (ii) a CACHE_AND_REVALIDATE arm that binds a stable, agent-visible identifier of the gating object and must re-fetch it before replay, charged honestly; (iii) a MANDATORY null arm on a substrate where the only readable identifier is session-scoped or the only reachable path is discovered, which must produce a measurable wrong action or a measurable cost gap, and which MAY be preregistered in advance as a COST null instead of a WRONGNESS null if no credential-free site with CSRF or a write surface is reachable, so the null arm is never again vacuous on this substrate class; and (iv) a mandatory RE_VALIDATE arm that pays the re-fetch price, so break-even is measured rather than assumed.
